title: Platform systems & services integrated playbook (how-tos, dashboards, runbooks, roadmap) - 2026 Q3
author: Asha Menon
content:
Overview

This integrated playbook consolidates platform systems & services guidance: operational runbooks, dashboard and alert standards, common how-tos, retrospective findings, and the near-term roadmap. The audience is platform engineers, SREs, oncall responders, and partner teams (infra, serving-runtime, product).

Scope

- Applies to the Platform Systems & Services team responsibilities: dashboards, alerting, runbooks, incident response, and platform-level roadmaps.
- Includes runbooks for high-impact incidents (latency SLO breaches, GPU OOMs, autoscaler misbehavior), how-tos for dashboard creation and alert tuning, and the Q3–Q4 2026 roadmap.

Owner & Escalation

- Primary owner: eng-platform (Platform Systems & Services)
- Document owner/author: Asha Menon (Platform Engineering)
- First oncall escalation: Platform SRE rotation (pager duty: team "eng-platform-oncall")
- Pager escalation matrix:
  1. oncall engineer (platform) – 15 minutes
  2. platform lead (Diego Ramirez) – 30 minutes
  3. eng-sre director (Mei Chen) – 60 minutes

Standards & Conventions

- Dashboard tooling: Grafana backed by Prometheus and Cortex for metrics, Loki for logs, Tempo for traces.
- Alerting platform: Alertmanager with route groups per severity and service. Critical alerts page to Slack channel #pager-platform and to phone pagers.
- Metric naming convention: service.component.metric (e.g., platform.cache.kv_hit_ratio)
- SLI/SLO defaults for platform services (unless service-specific SLO defined):
  - Availability SLO: 99.95% monthly (error-rate-based: 5xx or RPC timeout)
  - P99 latency: depends on service class; for API facing routes P99 target 300ms

How-tos (quick references)

1) Create a new Grafana dashboard (standard template)

- Steps:
  1. Duplicate the canonical dashboard template: "Platform Service Overview (template)" in Grafana.
  2. Replace datasource placeholders (Prometheus endpoint) with service-specific datasource.
  3. Update variables: service_name, environment (prod/staging), region.
  4. Add panels: CPU/GPU utilization, request rate, p50/p95/p99 latencies, error rate, queue length, KV cache hit ratio.
  5. Add links:
     - Runbook link (Confluence)
     - Playbook for incident response
  6. Save with name: platform.<service>.overview.<env>

- Typical panel queries:
  - request_rate: rate(platform_service_requests_total{service=~"$service_name", env=~"$environment"}[1m])
  - p99_latency: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(platform_service_request_duration_seconds_bucket{service="$service_name"}[5m])) by (le))

2) Add an alert rule (Alertmanager)

- Guidance:
  - Keep alerts actionable (if no one can remediate, convert to dashboarding/observability ticket).
  - Use a two-stage severity: warning (medium) threshold at 3 consecutive evaluation intervals, critical (pager) at 6 intervals.

- Example alert (YAML-style rule snippet):
alert: PlatformHighP99Latency
expr: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(platform_service_request_duration_seconds_bucket{service="my-service",env="prod"}[5m])) by (le)) > 1.2
for: 10m
labels:
  severity: page
annotations:
  summary: "P99 latency for my-service > 1.2s"
  runbook: "https://confluence.internal/eng-platform/runbooks/my-service-p99"

Dashboards & Alerts: Best practices

- Dashboard hygiene:
  - One overview dashboard per service + one team dashboard for aggregated health.
  - Panels should have clear thresholds and inline descriptions.
  - Use templating variables for environment/region to avoid duplicates.
- Alert hygiene:
  - Limit noisy alerts by using aggregated queries and burn-in periods (for e.g., 5–10m).
  - Annotate alerts with summary, impact, and runbook links.
  - Track alert noise via a weekly alert-rate dashboard; reduce top noisy alerts every sprint.

Runbooks (operational playbooks)

Included runbooks (links to Confluence pages):
- platform-high-latency-runbook (this file references the canonical runbook below)
- platform-gpu-oom-runbook
- platform-autoscaler-failure-runbook
- platform-cache-consistency-incident-runbook

Canonical runbook: platform-high-latency-runbook (summary)

- Trigger: Pager alert PlatformHighP99Latency fires (severity=page) or dashboard indicates sustained P99 above SLO for 15+ minutes.
- Impact assessment: Check services impacted list and customer-facing routes. Classify impact (sev1: global, sev2: region-specific, sev3: non-blocking).

Immediate steps (first 15 minutes):
1. Acknowledge alert in PagerDuty and post an incident thread to #incident-platform with short TL;DR.
2. Run quick triage commands:
# Check autoscaler status
kubectl -n platform get hpa,myautoscaler -o wide
# Check downstream queue length
kubectl -n platform exec -it svc/queue-metrics -- curl /metrics | grep queue_length
# Check GPU utilization
promql: sum by(instance)(gpu_utilization{service="$service_name"})

3. If CPU/GPU saturation found: scale up replica count or temporarily route traffic to warm pool (see routing playbook).
4. If increased error rates: identify error class (5xx vs timeouts) and roll back recent deploy if correlated.

Remediation & Recovery (15–60 minutes):
- Autoscaler issues: roll back autoscaler config change or temporarily set a static replica count.
- Model-serving regression: fallback to previous model variant or degrade to smaller model flavor; inform product and serving-runtime.
- Cache stampede: enable read-through caching or temporarily increase TTL on cache.

Post-incident (within 48 hours):
- Create a post-incident ticket with timeline, root cause hypothesis, mitigations applied, and owner for follow-up.
- Schedule a 60–90 minute incident retro within 7 days.

Retrospectives: Template & recent findings

Retrospective template (run in retro meeting):
- Facts: timeline, services affected, key metrics (error rate, latency, user impact).
- Root cause analysis: contributing factors and primary root cause.
- Action items: clear owners, TLs, and deadlines (usually <30 days for critical fixes).
- Follow-up verification: metric/synthetic checks to validate the fix.

Recent common themes (Q2–Q3 2026):
- Noisy alerts due to narrow thresholds on p95/p99 for internal-only endpoints — action: standardize thresholds and move internal-only metrics to optional surveillance.
- Autoscaler misconfigurations after infra changes — action: add autoscaler config validation CI step and a pre-deploy smoke test.
- Insufficient metric cardinality on cache keys — action: reduce high-cardinality labels and introduce sampled tracing for hot-keys.

Roadmap (Q3–Q4 2026 priorities)

Short-term (next 90 days):
- Consolidate dashboard templates and roll out automated provisioning for service dashboards (infra ticket: PLAT-2345).
- Implement alert noise monitoring dashboard and an Alert Reduction sprint (owner: Owen Patel).
- Add autoscaler validation checks in deployment CI (owner: Eng Infra).

Medium-term (Q4 2026):
- Deploy a low-latency metrics aggregation path for P99 calculation to reduce query cost and improve alert accuracy.
- Work with eng-serving-runtime to implement per-model lightweight health probes and circuit breakers.
- Launch platform runbook certification: each service must have a validated runbook and a drill twice per year.

Long-term (2027 planning):
- Platform observability overhaul: unified trace sampling and a combined cost/latency dashboard per route (cost center attribution).
- Integrate synthetic workloads with Canary engine for pre-deploy SLO validation.

Team wiki & onboarding

- Onboarding checklist for new platform engineers:
  1. Read this playbook and the SLO/SLA docs.
  2. Complete Grafana & Prometheus basics training (internal course: "Observability 101").
  3. Shadow oncall for two weeks and complete two runbook drills.
  4. Add your name to service ownership pages and verify runbook links.

- Useful wiki links (quick):
  - Platform team calendar (maintenance windows)
  - Grafana templates library
  - Alert tuning guide
  - Incident review playbook

Appendix: Configuration & requirements table

Item | Required value / recommended | Notes
------|------------------------------|-------
Metrics retention | 90 days (metrics), 365 days (aggregates) | Long-tail analytics retained but rollups only after 30d
Alert evaluation interval | 1m | Use 3 consecutive intervals for warning, 6 for critical
Default SLOs | Availability 99.95% / P99 per-route defined | Services may tighten per-customer SLAs
Dashboard template path | grafana/templates/platform-service-overview.json | Stored in Git (repo: infra/grafana-templates)
